summary: A 1974 note describing an approved scheme for connecting host computers to the network through host ports. It deals with the practical question of how a host attaches to the network. Its status is unknown.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 667 publishes BBN's approved host-port configuration for connecting computers and devices to the network. Its diagram shows which hosts connect to which IMPs and lists their host numbers.

subtitle: An approved BBN scheme for connecting host computers to IMPs.

tldr.problem: BBN needed an approved configuration showing how its computers and devices would connect to the network.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC diagrams hosts attached to IMP-50 and IMP-5 and gives host numbers in decimal and octal notation.
tldr.outcome: The configuration was scheduled to take effect December 18, 1974; the note also explains why host 105 was assigned to the line-printer PDP-11.

today: RFC 667 is a 1974 record of an approved BBN host-port configuration.

sections.title: The BBN Host-Port Diagram
sections.content:
The RFC presents an approved scheme for connecting BBN computers to the network, effective December 18, 1974. Its diagram shows PDP-10 and PDP-11 systems and special-purpose devices connected through IMP-50 and IMP-5, as well as connections to other listed network equipment.

Host identifiers in the diagram are shown in decimal and octal notation.
sections.plainLanguage: The diagram shows BBN's computers and devices and the IMPs they connect through. Each host has a number written in decimal and octal.

sections.title: Host Interface Notes
sections.content:
The RFC says all host interfaces are local, except host number 005, which could be converted between local and distant operation. BBN had been asked not to use 005 so Division 6 could more easily check PDP-10 IMP interfaces.

The PDP-11 with the line printer was intentionally assigned host 105. A simple program on it could answer a connection to its logger socket with the host number to use to log in to BBN System C.
sections.plainLanguage: Most interfaces were local. Host 005 was left available for interface testing, while the line-printer PDP-11 was given a number that could direct users to System C.

sections.title: Effective Date
sections.content: The approved configuration was scheduled to become effective December 18, 1974. The RFC documents the arrangement and the reason for the host 105 assignment.
sections.plainLanguage: The note states when the approved configuration would take effect. It also explains the intended use of host 105.
